niche_preference_profile: This user prefers clean, modern, app-like interfaces that feel complete and immediately usable. They like light or airy screens when the content is informational or settings-based, but they also respond well to dark, premium modal treatments when the dialog is focused and uncluttered. Across contexts, they favor clear hierarchy, explicit sectioning, visible actions, and enough content density to avoid empty or unfinished-looking screens. They dislike decorative clutter, oversized hero imagery, vague labels, and layouts that feel sparse, fragmented, or overly promotional.

criteria.description: The user prefers screens with a strong top-to-bottom hierarchy, clear section separation, and obvious emphasis on the most important content.
The user prefers layouts that feel open and breathable, but still sufficiently filled with content so they do not look empty, unfinished, or sparse.
The user prefers interfaces that show a fuller set of settings, items, or options on-screen rather than hiding key content or leaving sections blank.
The user prefers restrained, product-focused UI without large hero images, excessive banners, extra chrome, or visually distracting background elements.
The user prefers obvious interactive controls, including visible primary actions, toggles, chevrons, and per-item actions that make the screen feel usable.
The user prefers short, direct, task-focused wording over verbose, promotional, or overly instructional copy.
The user prefers interfaces that feel refined, contemporary, and finished rather than rough, dated, utilitarian, or placeholder-like.
The user prefers content organized into clearly named groups with explicit labels that make the structure easy to scan and understand.
The user prefers a calm, friendly, reassuring tone over urgent, alarming, or harsh presentation, especially in modal and alert flows.
